READ-ONLY audit of Nxeon (/opt/nxeon) covering EMAIL DELIVERABILITY, LEGAL/COMPLIANCE, and CUSTOMER-FACING TRUST. Do NOT edit/build/mutate — investigation only.

1. **Transactional email deliverability** (critical — if these don't land, customers miss invoices/resets/alerts): trace lib/mailer.ts + how mail is sent (SMTP? Mailcow?). Verify: are outgoing mails DKIM-signed? SPF/DMARC aligned? A prior note says the real DKIM record was deleted and mail runs through Mailcow (keys must come from Mailcow's API, not the local resolver) — investigate the CURRENT state: is there a DKIM selector/record configured, is mail signed, will invoice/password-reset/verification emails reach an inbox or spam? Check the actual sender domain (nxeon.cloud) config in the repo/settings. Report what's verifiable from here and what needs a live DNS/Mailcow check.
2. **Which transactional emails exist + fire**: signup verification, password reset, invoice/receipt, renewal reminder, dunning, provision-complete, cancellation. Any missing or unwired?
3. **Legal/compliance**: presence + adequacy of Terms, Privacy, Refund/AUP pages (app/legal/*), cookie consent, and — since VAT is now CHARGED — whether invoicing/ToS reflect VAT (VAT-ID capture, credit notes, EU reverse-charge). GDPR basics (data export/delete).
4. **Trust signals**: the Trustpilot/Google review badges (components/marketing/ReviewBadges.tsx) currently show DEMO placeholders — confirm they auto-switch to real approved reviews and there's no fabricated hard number shipped as fact.

Deliverable: findings ranked HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW with file:line, what a customer/regulator would see, and fix. Clearly separate "verifiable in code" vs "needs a live DNS/Mailcow/prod check by the owner."

# Nxeon audit — Email deliverability, Legal/Compliance, Trust (READ-ONLY)

## Environment facts pulled live from the DB `Setting` table (verifiable)
- `smtp_host = 10.20.0.10`, `smtp_port = 587`, `smtp_secure = false` (STARTTLS), `smtp_user` set, `smtp_from = "Nxeon <noreply@nxeon.cloud>"` → transactional mail **is** configured and routes through the Mailcow VM (10.20.0.10), authenticated. `mailConfigured()` is true, so invoices/resets will attempt to send (not the silent-failure scenario).
- `seller_country = UNSET`, `tax_percent = UNSET`.
- `review_url_* = UNSET`, **approved external reviews = 0**.
- External DNS egress is blocked from this box (couldn't even resolve google.com TXT), so **all SPF/DKIM/DMARC DNS checks for nxeon.cloud must be done live by the owner.**

---

## HIGH

**H1 — Fabricated review numbers ship as fact on the live homepage & pricing page.**
`components/marketing/ReviewBadges.tsx:29-33` defines `DEMO_BADGES` (Trustpilot 4.9/312, HostAdvice 4.8/148, Google 4.9/205). With 0 approved reviews (confirmed in DB), `ReviewBadges()` (`:91-94`) falls back to these and renders them on `app/page.tsx:152` and `app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx:190`. **The rendered output carries NO visible "demo" label** — the code comment claims "clearly-labelled DEMO PLACEHOLDER" but the JSX (`:96-120`) shows only stars + score + count, and the `aria-label` (`:104`) literally announces *"4.9 out of 5 on Trustpilot — 312 reviews"*. Links are `href="#"`. A customer/regulator sees invented Trustpilot/Google ratings presented as genuine (misleading-advertising + Trustpilot/Google brand misuse). The auto-switch to real data works correctly; the defect is that the fallback is unlabeled. *Fix: add a visible "sample/demo" tag or don't render numeric scores/counts until real reviews exist.*

**H2 — VAT is charged from a hardcoded rate table with no seller registration configured and no VAT number on invoices.**
`lib/tax.ts:134-139` (`COUNTRY_VAT_RATES`) is applied to any customer whose `billingCountry` is an EU-27/UK code, wired into both the order path (`lib/order.ts:34,591-602`) and renewals (`worker/billing.ts:26,258-385`). It is **not gated by any enable flag**. Because `seller_country` is UNSET, `resolveCountryTaxRate` (`lib/tax.ts:191-215`) treats every valid-format EU VAT ID as a cross-border reverse charge (`country !== ""` always true) and charges destination consumer VAT to everyone else. So a customer selecting "Germany" is charged 19% "VAT", the invoice line reads `VAT / Tax (19% · DE)` (`lib/invoices.ts:472-475`) — **but no seller VAT registration number appears anywhere on the invoice** (grep confirms none), and there's no check that the business is registered / has crossed an OSS threshold. Collecting VAT you may not be registered for, on invoices lacking a VAT number, is a serious regulator-facing exposure. *Fix: gate VAT collection behind a "VAT registered" flag + `seller_country`, and print the seller VAT number on every taxed invoice.*

**H3 — Transactional DKIM signing is not done in the app; depends entirely on Mailcow + DNS that can't be verified here.**
`lib/mailer.ts` builds the nodemailer transport (`:66-83`) with **no DKIM options** — signing must happen at the Mailcow relay (10.20.0.10). The platform has a DKIM self-check for *customer* email-hosting domains (`lib/mailcow.ts:466 mcGetDkimDetails`) but **nothing verifies the platform's own `nxeon.cloud` sending domain** is present on Mailcow, has a live DKIM key, and has SPF/DKIM/DMARC published. Per your memory note, the real DKIM record was previously deleted. **NEEDS LIVE CHECK:** (a) `mcGetDkimDetails("nxeon.cloud")` returns a key; (b) `dig TXT dkim._domainkey.nxeon.cloud`, `dig TXT nxeon.cloud` (SPF includes Mailcow), `dig TXT _dmarc.nxeon.cloud`; (c) send a probe and inspect Authentication-Results for `dkim=pass spf=pass dmarc=pass`. If nxeon.cloud isn't signed, every invoice/password-reset/verification email risks spam/reject. `scripts/diag-email.ts` exists as a send-probe helper.

---

## MEDIUM

**M1 — Six built transactional templates are never emailed (only shown in the admin preview).** Confirmed 0 live email fires for each: `provisioned`, `suspended`, `renewalWarning`, `passwordChanged`, `domainRenewed`, `invoiceNew`. Most impactful:
- **`provisioned`** — server-ready/SSH-access email never sent; success is only an in-app `notify()` (`worker/index.ts:471`). Only `provisionFailed` is emailed (`:783`).
- **`suspended`** — suspension writes an audit log (`worker/billing.ts:1044`, `worker/product-renewals.ts:264,390`) but sends the customer no email at the moment of suspension (pre-suspension dunning emails do fire).
- **`passwordChanged`** — no "your password was changed" security email after a reset (`lib/actions-account.ts` fires the reset *link* at `:155/226` but never the confirmation). Missing account-takeover safeguard.
*Wired-and-firing correctly:* welcome, email verification, password-reset link, receipt, and the full card-dunning sequence (paymentFailed/RetryFailed/ActionRequired/FinalNotice/Receipt/cardExpiringSoon via `worker/billing.ts:199`).

**M2 — Terms of Service contradict the fact that VAT is now collected.** `app/legal/terms/page.tsx:43` states *"Prices are stated exclusive of any applicable taxes, which you are responsible for."* — the platform now itself charges/collects VAT. The ToS (last updated "July 23, 2026") also **names no legal entity, registered address, or VAT number**, and governing law is a placeholder (`:100` "should be finalized with legal counsel"). *Fix: update tax clause + add legal-entity/VAT identity block.*

**M3 — Reverse-charge invoices are not legally labeled and VAT IDs are only format-checked.** A 0% reverse-charged invoice stores `taxCents:0` and renders just "Tax $0.00" — no *"VAT reverse charged — customer to account for VAT"* note and **no buyer VAT ID printed** (required for EU B2B). Additionally `isValidVatIdFormat` (`lib/tax.ts:154-161`) is a regex only, **not a VIES lookup** (acknowledged in the comment), so a structurally-valid but fake ID gets 0% and the seller eats the liability.

**M4 — No dedicated Refund/withdrawal policy page.** `app/legal/` has only `terms`, `privacy`, `aup`, `sla`. Refund terms are one inline ToS line ("fees are non-refundable… at our discretion"). For EU consumers this omits the digital-services right-of-withdrawal disclosure. *(Credit notes on server-refund do exist in code — `lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:413-435`.)*

**M5 — GDPR "export" is only a count summary, not a data export.** `lib/actions-gdpr.ts:30-46 exportSummary` returns *counts* (servers, invoices, tickets…), not a machine-readable download of the user's personal data — the data-portability right isn't actually fulfilled. Account deletion (`deleteMyAccount:60-117`) is properly implemented (email confirm, blocks on active servers, anonymizes audit trail).

---

## LOW

**L1 — Stale/misleading doc comment in `lib/tax.ts:76-89`** states the rate "IS NOT CHARGED TO ANYONE," but `taxContextForUser` (`:222`) uses `taxRate()` as the fallback percent, so it can be charged. Update the comment (it also references deleting a `BillingPanel.tsx` note that should now be revisited).

**L2 — No cancellation/account-closed email** exists at all (no template, no fire); `deleteMyAccount` just redirects. Minor trust gap.

**L3 — Cookie consent is opt-out** (`components/marketing/CookieConsent.tsx`) — analytics cookies may set before an explicit choice; acceptable for many jurisdictions but not strict-EU-clean. Banner links to the privacy policy and offers "Necessary only" (good).

1. `mcGetDkimDetails("nxeon.cloud")` returns a key + published `dkim._domainkey.nxeon.cloud` TXT (H3).
2. `dig TXT nxeon.cloud` (SPF authorizes Mailcow 10.20.0.10 / its public IP) and `dig TXT _dmarc.nxeon.cloud` (H3).
3. Send probe via `scripts/diag-email.ts` to a Gmail/Outlook address → confirm `dkim=pass / spf=pass / dmarc=pass` in headers (H3).
4. Confirm whether the business is actually VAT-registered before H2's collection continues.
